import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from io import StringIO

# Create the dataset
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR"""

df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(data))

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))
fig.suptitle('Camera Dataset Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Color palette for brands
brand_colors = {'Leica': '#E31837', 'Fuji': '#00A651', 'Pentax': '#0066B3', 'Olympus': '#FFD700'}

# 1. Price vs Megapixels scatter plot
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 1)
for brand in df['brand'].unique():
    brand_data = df[df['brand'] == brand]
    ax1.scatter(brand_data['megapixels'], brand_data['price_usd'], 
                s=brand_data['weight_grams']/5, alpha=0.7, 
                c=brand_colors[brand], label=brand, edgecolors='black', linewidth=1)
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Price vs Megapixels\n(bubble size = weight)', fontsize=12)
ax1.legend(title='Brand', loc='upper left')
ax1.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 2. Bar chart - Price by Brand
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 2)
brand_prices = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
bars = ax2.barh(brand_prices.index, brand_prices.values, 
                color=[brand_colors[b] for b in brand_prices.index], edgecolor='black')
ax2.set_xlabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Average Price by Brand', fontsize=12)
ax2.bar_label(bars, fmt='$%.0f', padding=3)
ax2.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='x')

# 3. Sensor Type Distribution (Pie chart)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 3)
sensor_counts = df['sensor_type'].value_counts()
colors_pie = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(sensor_counts)))
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax3.pie(sensor_counts, labels=sensor_counts.index, 
                                    autopct='%1.0f%%', colors=colors_pie,
                                    explode=[0.05]*len(sensor_counts),
                                    shadow=True, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Sensor Type Distribution', fontsize=12)

# 4. Model Year vs Max ISO with body type markers
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(2, 2, 4)
body_markers = {'Compact': 'o', 'Mirrorless': 's', 'DSLR': '^'}
for idx, row in df.iterrows():
    ax4.scatter(row['model_year'], row['max_iso'], 
                c=brand_colors[row['brand']], 
                marker=body_markers[row['body_type']], 
                s=150, edgecolors='black', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.8)

# Create custom legend for body types
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], marker=m, color='w', markerfacecolor='gray', 
                          markersize=10, label=bt, markeredgecolor='black') 
                   for bt, m in body_markers.items()]
ax4.legend(handles=legend_elements, title='Body Type', loc='upper left')
ax4.set_xlabel('Model Year', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Max ISO', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Max ISO by Model Year\n(color = brand, shape = body type)', fontsize=12)
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax4.set_yscale('log')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white')
plt.close()
